persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Dave Kowalski, 58. You run Kowalski Builders, a three-person general construction company outside Chicago — garages, additions, decks. Your quotes live on the back of lumber-yard receipts, deposits get written in a notebook, and every April you hand your accountant a shoebox. Today you want one place on your phone for customers, prices, quotes and who has paid.

challenge.intro: Now you are Dave with Kowalski Builders. The app is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press — use what you learned. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Business Manager with the normal link. If you see the 'Welcome to Business Manager' card, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' — it is already empty, begin. If you see 'Run the business from your phone' with 'Set it up for my business (2 min) →', it is already empty too — begin. Otherwise tap ⚙️ More at the bottom right, scroll down and tap '🗑️ Erase everything and start over' → OK → OK. You should now see 'Run the business from your phone'.

tasks.text: Set the app up for your company: Kowalski Builders, your name Dave Kowalski, general construction work, office phone 847-555-0100.
tasks.hint: The set-up chat asks for the business name, your name, the kind of work and your phone. Pick 🏗️ General Construction. You can stop early with 'Skip — turn everything on' and then 'Let’s go →'. Already set up with the wrong kind of work? ⚙️ More → Business info.

tasks.text: You charge $11 a square foot for framing — not the starting price. Fix it so every quote uses $11.
tasks.hint: The prices every quote uses live in ⚙️ More → Price list. Find the Framing row and change its price.

tasks.text: Ruth Novak called about a garage: 847-555-0167, 905 Elm St, Libertyville. Save her as a customer.
tasks.hint: The round + New button at the bottom can add a customer. Put her phone number in the Phone box.

tasks.text: Price Ruth's job: 600 square feet of framing plus a dumpster. The total must come to $7,150.
tasks.hint: Start a new job for Ruth, then add lines from your price list. The ⚡ draft only puts 1 of each and may add lines you did not ask for — tap a line to change how many or to remove it. 600 × $11 = $6,600, plus $550.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('bizmgr_v1')||'null');if(!d||!d.setup||!d.setup.done||d.setup.demo)return false;var dg=function(s){return String(s||'').replace(/\D/g,'').slice(-10)};var ids=(d.customers||[]).filter(function(c){return /ruth/i.test(c.name)&&/novak/i.test(c.name)}).map(function(c){return c.id});var js=(d.jobs||[]).filter(function(j){return ids.indexOf(j.customerId)>=0});return js.some(function(j){var it=j.items||[],t=0;it.forEach(function(l){t+=parseFloat(l.qty)*parseFloat(l.price)});var fr=it.some(function(l){return /framing/i.test(l.name)&&Math.abs(parseFloat(l.qty)-600)<0.001&&Math.abs(parseFloat(l.price)-11)<0.001});var du=it.some(function(l){return /dumpster|haul/i.test(l.name)&&Math.abs(parseFloat(l.qty)*parseFloat(l.price)-550)<0.001});return fr&&du&&Math.abs(t-7150)<0.01})}catch(e){return false}})()

tasks.text: Ruth said yes and handed you a check for the 30% deposit ($2,145). Mark the job approved and record her check.
tasks.hint: On the job, '👍 They said yes' marks it approved. Under BILLING, 'Deposit (30%)' makes the deposit invoice; on it, '💵 Record a payment' — set How to Check. Never press a 📨 Send button.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('bizmgr_v1')||'null');if(!d||!d.setup||!d.setup.done||d.setup.demo)return false;var dg=function(s){return String(s||'').replace(/\D/g,'').slice(-10)};var ids=(d.customers||[]).filter(function(c){return /ruth/i.test(c.name)&&/novak/i.test(c.name)}).map(function(c){return c.id});var js=(d.jobs||[]).filter(function(j){return ids.indexOf(j.customerId)>=0});return js.some(function(j){if(!j.signed||['approved','scheduled','working','done','closed'].indexOf(j.status)<0)return false;var paid=0;(d.invoices||[]).forEach(function(v){if(v.jobId===j.id)(v.payments||[]).forEach(function(p){if(/check/i.test(p.method))paid+=parseFloat(p.amount)})});return Math.abs(paid-2145)<0.01})}catch(e){return false}})()

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: keeps customers, jobs, quotes and invoices for a small trade business on your phone
prices quotes from your own price list
tracks deposits, payments, expenses and what each job really made
reminds you of to-dos and tax due dates

lines: Business Manager is an office for a small trade business that fits in your phone. There is no video for it yet, so here it is in plain words.
It is made for one-truck and small-crew businesses: plumbers, painters, roofers, and general contractors like you.
The first time you open it, a short welcome card offers a tour. You can look around a pretend business, Miller Plumbing, or start fresh with your own.
Starting fresh is a short chat: your business name, your name, what you need, the kind of work you do and your phone number. It takes about two minutes.
When you pick your kind of work, the app fills in a starting price list. For General Construction it has framing, concrete, drywall, a dumpster, equipment rental and more.
Those are only starting prices. Change them to yours in More, then Price list. Every quote uses your prices.
Customers are saved with their phone and address, so you never have to look them up again.
A job is the work for one customer. You add lines from your price list — for example, 600 square feet of framing at eleven dollars, plus a dumpster — and it adds up the total for you.
The lightning button drafts a price from your price list in one tap. Check it: it puts one of each, so change the amounts to the real job.
When the customer says yes, tap They said yes. The job moves along: approved, scheduled, working, done, paid.
Under Billing you can make a deposit invoice, a progress bill, or the final invoice. When the money comes in, record the payment and say how it was paid.
The Money tab shows money in, money out and your real profit, job by job, and how much to set aside for taxes.
Expenses like a lumber bill can be tied to a job, so you see what that job really made.
The to-do list holds your own reminders, and with one tap it adds the usual tax dates, truck and insurance renewals.
Everything stays on this phone. Nothing is sent unless you press a Send button — and in this test, never press one.
To clear it all, go to More, then Erase everything and start over. It asks twice first.
